This module introduces no new CFR (Code of Federal Regulations) citation and no new external
source. It's pure synthesis — placing a clause module 4 already quoted in full against a process
`quality-system-essentials` already taught in depth — so no new sourcing was needed or attempted
this session.

**Internal links, not external sources:**

- **[Business Associate Agreements](../business-associate-agreements/index.qmd)** — module 4. The
  full, verbatim text of 45 CFR 164.314(a)(2)(i)(C) and 164.504(e)(2)(ii)(C) — the incident-
  reporting clause this module builds its reactive-vs-proactive distinction on — lives there, quoted
  from `sources/cfr/45-164-business-associate-excerpt.md`. This module deliberately doesn't re-quote
  it at length; go back to module 4 for the full paragraph and the complete (e)(2)(ii)(A)–(J)
  checklist walkthrough.
- **[Change control for regulated systems](../../quality-system-essentials/change-control-for-
  regulated-systems/index.qmd)** — `quality-system-essentials`, module 4. The five-stage process
  (request, impact and risk assessment, approval, implementation, verification) that governs changes
  to Lakeshore's own BECS (Blood Establishment Computer Software) and eQMS (electronic quality
  management system) is taught there in full and referenced, not redeveloped, here. Read it (or
  re-read it) for the mechanics this module assumes you already have.
- **[Reading an ISO 27001 Certificate](../reading-an-iso-27001-certificate/index.qmd)** — module 3.
  Its Statement of Applicability finding on the vendor's plausible "change management" control
  domain is the internal-governance half of this module's central distinction; this module's other
  half is the contractual-notice question, which that domain doesn't answer.
- **[Investigating a Healthcare Data Incident](../../healthcare-security-and-privacy/investigating-
  a-healthcare-data-incident/index.qmd)** — the closed incident this course has used as its running
  example throughout, and the source of the root-cause finding (the deployment-sequencing gap) this
  module's change-notification discussion is built to address going forward, without reopening or
  altering that course's own final determination.

If a future session wants to verify this module's reasoning against a real AICPA, ISO, or HHS
(Department of Health and Human Services) source, the relevant sourcing notes are already recorded
in modules 2–4's own `resources.qmd` files and in this course's plan file
(`plans/vendor-and-third-party-risk-management.md`) — nothing further was fetched for this closing
module.
